jobs.description:
Our Mission:
Hospital-Quality Care, Everywhere.

The healthcare industry still relies on faxes and phone tags to coordinate critical care for patients at home. We think patients and the clinicians who serve them deserve better than a system stuck in 1995.

Verse Medical is building the modern software infrastructure to make it happen. We're a well-funded Series C company (backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, and Sapphire Ventures) on a mission to heal a fragmented system. Our platform connects the dots between providers, payors, and patients, ensuring people get the high-quality care they need, reliably and right where they live. We’re growing fast and looking for people who are driven by this mission to join us!

Our Values:
The Principles That Guide Us

Our values are the operating system for how we work together and with our partners. They aren't just words on a wall; they are the principles we bring to every decision, every day.

We are transparent, upfront and direct. We operate with honesty and clarity. We share information openly, the good and the bad, and believe that direct, respectful feedback is the foundation of trust and progress.
We value speed of iteration. We are building something new, which means we learn by doing. We prioritize rapid iteration and getting solutions into the hands of users, believing that progress is more valuable than perfection.
We give 110% effort, 30% of the time. We are passionate about our mission, and there are moments that require us to go the extra mile. We believe in focused intensity when it counts, balanced by a sustainable pace that keeps our team energized for the long run.
We empathize with customers to a fault. When our users face a problem, we own it. Instead of asking them to change, we ask ourselves, "How can we make this better?" We believe true innovation comes from deep empathy and a relentless focus on solving the real-world challenges of healthcare.

We’re hiring a Data Analyst
to turn Verse's data into decisions. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role where you'll partner directly with functional leaders to build the metrics, dashboards, and analyses that drive how the business operates. Not only are you offering the “what,” but also the “why” and the “what now,” translating messy, ambiguous business questions into clear, defensible, self-serve analytical assets.

If you enjoy high ownership, solving open-ended business problems with data, and having direct influence on a mission-driven company’s trajectory, this role is for you.

What You'll Achieve: A Glimpse into Your Contributions

Spearhead end-to-end analytics across business domains.
Understand trends in operational and customer data to influence how teams prioritize their own roadmaps
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Ops, Product, Leadership) to define new metrics, standardize reporting, and surface insights proactively.
Automate recurring reporting and manual data-quality checks using Python and SQL, reducing turnaround time on regular audits and deliverables.
Design and build algorithms/models (e.g., scoring, classification, similarity, or risk-adjustment models) that solve specific business problems, from provider mapping to fraud detection to cost-of-care scoring.

What You'll Bring: The Skills and Experience You’ll Leverage

We believe that diverse experiences and backgrounds lead to better solutions. While we have an idea of what will help someone succeed in this role, we are open to being convinced by your unique story and skills. If you believe you can achieve the outcomes above, we encourage you to apply.

Core Skills & Experience:

3+ years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or analytics engineering, with experience owning reporting and metrics end-to-end.
Strong experience writing SQL and Python for analysis, automation, and lightweight modeling
Experience building and driving adoption of dashboards (Metabase, Looker Tableau, PowerBI, or similar)
Experience developing custom metrics, scoring algorithms, or classification models to solve specific business problems.
Experience performing exploratory analysis with minimal direction on ambiguous, open-ended business questions
Proactive communicator with experience working with stakeholders
Preferred: Experience with dbt modeling.
Preferred: Experience with Snowflake.
Preferred: Familiarity with healthcare or other regulated data (HIPAA compliance).
Preferred: Experience working closely with engineers to triage and resolve issues.

Benefits:

Competitive compensation.
Opportunities for rapid career advancement in a growing company.
100% premium coverage for health insurance.
401(k) with no matching at this time.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York office and will require you to be in the office 4x in a week.

Our Pledge for an Equitable Future

At Verse Medical, our mission is to deliver equitable, hospital-quality care to everyone, regardless of their background or where they live. We can only achieve this if our own team reflects the diversity of the patients we serve. We are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, where their contributions are valued, and where they can do their best work. We embrace diversity of all kinds: race, gender, age, religion, identity, experience. We are actively working to build a more inclusive and equitable world, starting from within our own walls. We are an equal opportunity employer.

We are also committed to providing a positive and accessible interview experience. If you require any accommodations to participate in our process, please contact us at recruiting@versemedical.com.

Personally inspect codebases, system architecture, infrastructure, and technical roadmaps to directly assess engineering quality — not solely through management interviews or self-reported documentation.

Risk Assessment & Reporting:

Provide a structured evaluation of technical debt, security gaps, operational risks, business interruption risks, and talent gaps, grounded in direct technical review.
Business/Investment Impact Quantification:

Translate technical findings into quantified business and investment impact — for example, identifying a specific technical issue that materially affects valuation — to directly inform deal decisions.

Validate findings against business assumptions and provide recommendations on critical areas requiring attention.

Produce detailed TDD reports covering product, people, technology, and processes, giving a complete, technically grounded overview of the target company's technical landscape.
Process Improvement:

Recommend best practices to enhance the efficiency and rigor of the due diligence process.
Stakeholder Communication:

Present findings and recommendations to investors, executives, and decision-makers clearly and actionably, including the business/financial implications of technical findings.

15+ years of hands-on technology experience, with a track record of remaining personally close to code, architecture, and implementation details (not purely a management or oversight background).

Deep expertise in software architecture, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, cybersecurity, and software development lifecycle (SDLC).
Strong, current engineering judgment — demonstrated ability to independently evaluate architecture quality without relying on management reports.
Strong understanding of technical debt, scalability challenges, and operational risks, with the ability to quantify their business and investment impact.
Experience with modern development stacks and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP).
Exceptional analytical and documentation skills, with experience writing due diligence reports that connect technical findings to financial/valuation outcomes.
Strong ability to communicate complex technical findings to non-technical stakeholders.
Fluency (written and verbal) in at least one of the following languages required: French, Finnish, Hungarian, or German.

Experience working with Private Equity, Venture Capital, or M&A teams.
Knowledge of regulatory compliance frameworks such as GDPR, ISO 27001, and SOC 2.
Experience leading technical integrations post-acquisition.

Cleans and disinfects collection chairs, counters, equipment, and other work surfaces according to established schedules and procedures.
Uses appropriate personal protective equipment and follows standard precautions during all patient-care and laboratory activities.
Handles and disposes of sharps, biohazardous materials, chemicals, and regulated waste safely and in accordance with established requirements.
Maintains continual awareness of the laboratory environment and promptly identifies and reports potential hazards or unsafe conditions. Follows established procedures for needlestick injuries, blood or body-fluid exposures, spills, emergencies, and incident reporting.
Helps maintain a safe, secure, and healthy patient-care environment by adhering to organizational standards, policies, and legal requirements.

Receives, organizes, rotates, and stocks supplies using applicable expiration-date and first-expire, first-out practices.
Checks collection supplies, reagents, and testing materials for proper storage, condition, lot numbers, and expiration dates.

Performs assigned daily opening and closing procedures for laboratory and specimen-collection areas.
Verifies that work areas, equipment, and supplies are clean, functional, properly stored, and ready for patient care.
Completes required refrigerator, freezer, and room-temperature checks, equipment checks, and laboratory logs.
Secures specimens, confidential records, supplies, equipment, and laboratory areas at the end of the workday.
Reports unresolved equipment, temperature, safety, supply, or specimen concerns to the appropriate laboratory or clinical personnel.

Documentation, Compliance, and Quality Assurance

Accurately documents specimen collection, processing, waived testing, and specimen disposition in the electronic medical record and applicable laboratory logs.
Maintains complete, accurate, and legible records required for patient care, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance.
Protects confidential health information and maintains patient privacy in accordance with HIPAA, FERPA, organizational policies, and applicable laws.
Complies with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including CLIA, OSHA, bloodborne-pathogen standards, and Student Health Services policies and procedures.
Participates in required training, competency assessments, continuing education, quality-assurance activities, audits, and inspections.

Identifies and reports documentation errors, specimen discrepancies, safety concerns, equipment problems, and potential regulatory issues.

Duties And Responsibilities

Under the supervision of a general Clinical Lab Scientist (CLS I & CLS II), performs the following: Phlebotomy, Specimen Collection, and Patient Care

Greets patients, verifies identity using approved identifiers, confirms laboratory orders, and prepares patients for specimen collection.
Explains collection procedures and provides instructions regarding fasting, timed collections, clean-catch urine specimens, and other testing requirements.
Performs venipuncture and capillary phlebotomy in accordance with established procedures and within the scope of applicable certification.
Selects the appropriate collection tube, container, specimen type, and required volume for each ordered test.
Collects blood, urine, and other authorized specimens while maintaining patient comfort, privacy, and safety.
Observes patients for adverse reactions, including dizziness or fainting, and follows established response and notification procedures.
Provides professional, compassionate, and student-centered service throughout the laboratory visit.

Specimen Processing, Storage, and Transport

Accurately labels specimens at the time of collection and verifies that identifiers match the laboratory order and accompanying documentation.
Determines whether testing will be performed in-house or sent to a reference laboratory.
Completes laboratory requisitions, labels, logs, and other required documentation accurately.
Processes specimens according to established requirements, including centrifuging, separating, aliquoting, packaging, and preparing specimens for testing or transport.
Preserves and stores specimens according to test-specific temperature, timing, light-protection, and stability requirements.
Maintains specimen integrity throughout collection, processing, storage, and transport.
Coordinates reference-laboratory pickups and ensures specimens are packaged and transported within established timeframes.
Identifies mislabeled, insufficient, compromised, leaking, or otherwise unacceptable specimens and promptly reports concerns to the appropriate laboratory or clinical personnel.

Waived Testing and Clinical Laboratory Support

Performs authorized CLIA-waived testing, such as urine dipsticks, hemoglobin A1C, glucose, pregnancy testing, and other approved tests, after completing required training and competency assessments.
Follows approved procedures and manufacturer instructions for test performance, quality control, documentation, and reporting.
Verifies that testing materials have been properly stored and are within their expiration dates before use.
Records reagent lot numbers, expiration dates, quality-control results, and patient test results accurately.
Documents test results in the electronic medical record or applicable laboratory information system.
Immediately refers abnormal, critical, questionable, or inconsistent results to the appropriate licensed clinical or laboratory professional.
Assists laboratory personnel with daily operations and performs other laboratory-support activities within the position’s authorized scope.

Cleaning, Infection Prevention, and Safety

Maintains clean, organized, secure, and appropriately prepared specimen-collection and laboratory work areas.
Cleans and disinfects collection chairs, counters, equipment, and other work surfaces according to established schedules and procedures.
Uses appropriate personal protective equipment and follows standard precautions during all patient-care and laboratory activities.
Handles and disposes of sharps, biohazardous materials, chemicals, and regulated waste safely and in accordance with established requirements.
Maintains continual awareness of the laboratory environment and promptly identifies and reports potential hazards or unsafe conditions. Follows established procedures for needlestick injuries, blood or body-fluid exposures, spills, emergencies, and incident reporting.
Helps maintain a safe, secure, and healthy patient-care environment by adhering to organizational standards, policies, and legal requirements.

Equipment, Inventory, and Opening/Closing Duties

Monitors phlebotomy and laboratory supplies to maintain sufficient inventory levels for daily operations.
Receives, organizes, rotates, and stocks supplies using applicable expiration-date and first-expire, first-out practices.
Checks collection supplies, reagents, and testing materials for proper storage, condition, lot numbers, and expiration dates.
Reports supply shortages and assists with preparing inventory or ordering requests.
Performs assigned daily opening and closing procedures for laboratory and specimen-collection areas.
Verifies that work areas, equipment, and supplies are clean, functional, properly stored, and ready for patient care.
Completes required refrigerator, freezer, and room-temperature checks, equipment checks, and laboratory logs.
Secures specimens, confidential records, supplies, equipment, and laboratory areas at the end of the workday.
Reports unresolved equipment, temperature, safety, supply, or specimen concerns to the appropriate laboratory or clinical personnel.

Documentation, Compliance, and Quality Assurance

Accurately documents specimen collection, processing, waived testing, and specimen disposition in the electronic medical record and applicable laboratory logs.
Maintains complete, accurate, and legible records required for patient care, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance.
Protects confidential health information and maintains patient privacy in accordance with HIPAA, FERPA, organizational policies, and applicable laws.
Complies with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including CLIA, OSHA, bloodborne-pathogen standards, and Student Health Services policies and procedures.
Participates in required training, competency assessments, continuing education, quality-assurance activities, audits, and inspections.
Completes required quality-control, temperature, maintenance, specimen, and corrective-action logs.
Identifies and reports documentation errors, specimen discrepancies, safety concerns, equipment problems, and potential regulatory issues.

Six to twelve months of related experience in a healthcare setting or equivalent combination of education and experience which provides the required knowledge and abilities.
Knowledge: General knowledge of clinical laboratory operations and equipment, including an understanding of, or the ability to quickly learn, laboratory safety and quality assurance practices and procedures. General knowledge of medical terminology pertinent to laboratory operations; applicable laws and regulations pertaining to clinical laboratory operations and patient confidentiality. Working knowledge of CLIA-waived testing procedures, methods, and criteria. Abilities: Ability to collect required specimens for and perform assigned CLIA-waived testing with required attention to accuracy and detail; perform phlebotomy using the appropriate equipment including venipuncture and capillary puncture; use applicable equipment and materials in performing laboratory tests; use applicable automated systems for maintaining and tracking laboratory and patient records; maintain patient confidentiality as required by applicable state and federal laws and regulations; maintain effective working relationships with practitioners and other health center support staff; and be sensitive to and communicate effectively with diverse patients.

Support project scope, requirements, schedules, budgets, design, and technical coordination
for civil engineering projects.
Perform complex civil engineering work for facility planning, design, construction, and site improvements
.
Provide technical direction to architects, consulting engineers, District staff, contractors, and inspectors.
Review civil plans, specifications, surveys, and technical documents for compliance with District standards, codes, and project requirements
.
Review site development elements including grading, paving, parking, streets, drainage, sewer, utilities, ADA improvements, and related infrastructure
.
Identify design conflicts and recommend or direct necessary revisions.
Develop and maintain civil engineering standards, guidelines, and specifications
.
Review site development studies, feasibility, and estimated costs for grading, utilities, streets, and other civil improvements.
Resolve civil engineering issues during construction and provide technical guidance on field conditions.

and consultants on permits and off-site improvements, including B-Permit/A-Permit work
.

from a recognized college or university.

on commercial or public agency projects.

Experience using AutoCAD
for civil engineering design.
Proficiency with standard office software, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Adobe
, and related applications.
